what: ask 5 / C-31 — a wonder in the blast, and how many die per ring. Target TOKYO (Japan, p1) at 23:26, pop 18, with a DISTRICT_WONDER at 23:25 one tile from the centre and two more wonders at 24:27 and 25:25. Rings 0-2 were filled with ONE Japanese unit per land tile before the strike (17 spawned + 1 already on the centre). Delivered by a UNIT_BOMBER based in a captured city 4 tiles away. Four draws, three of them from a reload of the same save lab2_nuke_pre at turn 124.

aim: 23:25 (the WONDER tile, one ring off the city centre)
survivors: every unit within 2 of 23:25 died; the six survivors at city-ring 2 (21:26, 21:27, 22:28, 23:28, 24:28) and city-ring 3 are exactly the plots 3 or more from 23:25

note: draw 1 repeated after a reload of the same save - IDENTICAL result

reads: THE WONDER IS NEVER PILLAGED. Three strikes, three confirmations, including DRAW 3 where the wonder at 23:25 was GROUND ZERO. Every other district inside the radius pillaged every time - city centre, Aqueduct, Industrial Zone, Theater, Neighborhood, Holy Site, Campus - while DISTRICT_WONDER at 23:25, 24:27, 23:23 and 25:25 read pillaged=false in every draw. A WONDER district is immune to nuclear pillage.

the kill is NOT a proportion: it is 100% inside the blast radius and 0% outside, with a sharp cutoff at the radius. Thermonuclear (radius 2) killed 1/1, 7/7, 14/14 in rings 0,1,2 and left ring 3 untouched; the nuclear device (radius 1) killed 1/1 and 7/7 in rings 0,1 and left ALL 14 of ring 2 alive and undamaged. No survivor anywhere inside, no casualty anywhere outside, no partial damage on any unit.

draws 1 and 4 are the same strike from the same reloaded save and gave byte-identical outcomes (pop 18 -> 4, same kills). Neither the kill nor the population loss is rolled - C-31's 'proportion' reading is wrong for the units; they die outright.

the footprint is centred on the TARGET PLOT, not on the city. Draw 3 aimed one tile off the centre and the 19 contaminated plots were centred on 23:25, killing what was within 2 of THAT tile and sparing six units at city-ring 2 that a centred strike had killed.

population loss depends on the weapon and on where the blast lands relative to the city centre, and it is deterministic: centred thermonuclear 18 -> 4 (-14, twice), centred nuclear device 18 -> 15 (-3), thermonuclear one tile off centre 18 -> 11 (-7). Three points, not enough to separate 'a fraction per ring covered' from 'a fraction of the pop scaled by radius' - the ONE half of ask 5 this session could not close.

every improvement inside the radius is pillaged (Farm, Mine, Pasture, Quarry all read IsImprovementPillaged true afterwards and false before); improvements outside are untouched. Routes were not pillaged.

the struck city is NOT destroyed or captured: the city centre reads pillaged=true with garrison 200/200 and outer 300/300 - both pools at MAXIMUM damage, i.e. zero health - and the city still stands, still owned by Japan, producing nothing.

Gathering Storm has NO FEATURE_FALLOUT row - GameInfo.Features['FEATURE_FALLOUT'] is nil and a whole-map feature scan finds nothing. Contamination is its own manager: Game.GetFalloutManager():GetFalloutTurnsRemaining(plotIndex). The contaminated footprint is EXACTLY the blast rings (19 plots = 1+6+12 for radius 2, 7 plots = 1+6 for radius 1) and the duration is 20 turns for the thermonuclear device and 10 for the nuclear device, uniform across every plot. It is applied on the strike turn (draw 2 and draw 3 read it immediately).

Game.GetFalloutManager() also carries GetReactorCount, GetReactorByIndex, GetReactorAge, GetReactorAccidentThreshold, GetFalloutDamageOverride, GetFalloutPreventsWork and HasFallout - that is SCENE F's (ask 4) reader, found for free. A per-plant accident watch needs no new plumbing, only a save with plants.

delivery: a bomber can only be CREATED on a tile the player owns a city on - Create returned nil on open ground and in a foreign city, and succeeded on player 0's own city centre. Bomber Range is 10 and the strike is refused past it (dist 15 gave canStrike=false), so the scene needed a captured city 4 tiles from the target.
techs: Players[0]:GetTechs():SetTech(r.Index, true) over GameInfo.Technologies() granted all 77 in one call

what: Network.LoadGame WORKS from Lua but is NOT unattended - it stops on a Start Game button the OWNER must click
call: Network.LoadGame({Location=SaveLocations.LOCAL_STORAGE, Type=SaveTypes.SINGLE_PLAYER, IsAutosave=false, IsQuicksave=false, Directory=SaveDirectories.DEFAULT, Name='<save>'}, ServerType.SERVER_TYPE_NONE) [InGame]
behaviour: the tuner socket drops during the transition and stays down until a human presses Start Game; after that the first probe still fails with a ConnectionResetError or a non-zero exit and the NEXT one succeeds at the saved turn. lab.py opens a fresh socket per command, so the recipe is: call load, WAIT FOR THE OWNER'S CLICK, then retry the next command once.
correction: this row first read 'needs no human click'. That was wrong and the mistake is worth keeping: I watched only my own side of the socket, saw one probe fail and the next succeed, and read the recovery as automatic. The owner was clicking Start Game each time, off-instrument. A reload costs the OWNER'S HAND, so a plan needing N reloads needs the owner present for N clicks - never treat it as an automatable loop.
